about: Labels given by the user, one scan at a time, looking at the images. Ground truth for the 55-scan test pool. The filenames are deliberately uninformative or deliberately wrong: nothing here may be inferred from a name.

labels.label: calibration grating
labels.note: Certified pitch, so this scan is the reference against which the periodicity measurement itself is checked. Measured 1.7 um at 90 deg; grating model not yet confirmed by the user.

labels.label: scalpel scratch through a film, for film thickness
labels.note: User: 'misura molto frequente'. A scalpel cut down to the substrate; the film thickness is the step from the plateau to the trench floor. Bimodality 0.51, kurtosis -1.0: two height levels. Periodicity reports 28 at 101 deg, which is a FALSE POSITIVE -- one straight edge across the frame, not a repeat.

labels.label: halide perovskite crystal on a flat substrate
labels.note: One large faceted crystal about 5 x 15 um and 450 nm tall, plus lower ragged material and isolated debris. Periodicity reports 51 with a 102 nm period against a 48.9 nm pixel -- a FALSE POSITIVE at the two-pixel limit, i.e. line noise.
labels.user_note: The curved background here is the z feedback landing/flying over the tall crystal, not sample shape. This is the artifact we have to correct.

labels.label: unnamed -- genuine sample morphology, pitted surface
labels.note: User confirmed the image is good and everything in it is morphology; did not name the material. Flat surface, RMS 23 nm, pitted with holes 100-400 nm across and up to 8 nm deep. Skewness -1.97 catches it; the object count reports 0 in 0 pieces because the detector only looks for features ABOVE the background. I wrongly called the edge streaks a tip artifact -- they are real.

labels.label: same sample as index 4, different area
labels.note: User: 'si molto simile'. Same specimen, a few um away, but the descriptors land far apart: RMS 51 vs 23 nm, correlation length 566 vs 234 nm, skewness -0.37 vs -1.97. Pits still present; object count sees 2 pieces because it only looks upward. Elongated ridge-and-groove texture running up to the right.
